source.title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents
source.authors: Jun-Kai Lin; Ge Xu; Zheng Xu; Junkai Chen; Xiang-Yuan Lan

page_placements.theme: Agents, context memory and tools resupply or retain forgotten information

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests parameter-level unlearning and whether adding persistent memory or tool access changes answer recovery in an agent setting. It does not test the claim’s specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports token-level F1 for parametric, memory, tool, and combined agent conditions, including forget-set and retain-set results. These bear on version A’s forgetting, recovery, and utility components. The paper does not evaluate the specified recovery attacks individually, and it does not report a never-saw-knowledge control or a chance-level reference for F1. Table 2 reports tool-call, empty-output, and refusal rates; these help interpret agent performance but do not directly measure target-answer recovery, so they are not separate rows. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: On the TOFU forget05/retain95 splits, the paper measures how far GD, KL and NPO lower forget-set answer F1 and what they cost in retain-set F1, for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B (Table 1; Table 3 adds CIs). This bears on version A's forgetting and utility parts. Memory and tool conditions add external context. Sources conflict on whether that context holds the forget facts: the Fig. 1 caption says no, while Sec. 5.1 says the tool corpus uses the same profiles. So those rows cannot be read as recovery of hidden knowledge. None of the claim's recovery attacks (B–E) or a robust method (F) is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress two caveats: their results show answer recovery only, not whether information is erased from parameters or storage; and low tool-condition retain scores limit conclusions about tool-mediated recovery.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates GD, KL, and NPO on a TOFU-based agent benchmark with memory and offline web-tool conditions; it does not reproduce the specified fine-tuning, activation-edit, quantization, or prompting recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by backbone, unlearning method, and evaluation channel (Para., Mem., Tool, Final).

fits_no_version.finding: Adding Mem0 memory context raises forget-set F1 in 5 of 6 checkpoints (e.g. Qwen KL 16.8→30.1; complete agent 36.9). Tool access lowers F1 on both splits, with large empty-output and tool-invocation failures. Whether the memory or tool corpus contains the forget facts is stated inconsistently.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In agent systems, parameter-level unlearning is undermined by external memory or retrieval channels that resupply target answers; checkpoint-level forgetting does not predict system-level forgetting.

record.problems: Only two 8B model families, three methods, and the 5% TOFU forget setting are evaluated. Token-level F1 measures lexical overlap, not information removal. There is no reported retain-only or never-saw-knowledge comparison in the results, and no chance-level reference. Tool-condition F1 reductions coincide with substantial retain-set losses; Qwen3-8B also has empty-output and tool-invocation failures that complicate interpretation. Memory artifacts and web sources are fixed and controlled.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 2 rows for tool-call, empty-output, or refusal rates because they do not directly measure target-answer recovery or retained QA performance. Appendix Tables 3–4 and Figure 2 provide paired-difference, question-type, and illustrative response analyses; omitted to prioritize the main Table 1 condition-by-condition F1 results. No results cited from other work are included.

untested.parts: Near-chance comparison (no chance or retain-only oracle numbers reported despite the oracle being described); resistance to simple recovery attacks.
No activation ablation or blocked-versus-deleted analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak or other-language tests. Memory-context recovery cannot be attributed to hidden knowledge because memory provenance is contradictory.

record.verdict_notes: Provenance contradiction: the Fig. 1 caption says the memory bank and profile store hold no record of the forget entity. But Sec. 5.1 says the tool corpus is built from the same profiles as the memory, and the snapshot covers all 200 authors. The authors also say memory 'restores access to target knowledge'. Because of this conflict, the memory and tool rows are not mapped to E. The record's notes on Q-GD-FI-F and Q-NPO-FI-F misstate the text: for GD and NPO, forget F1 falls and retain F1 rises relative to parametric. The study names TOFU, not WMDP or HP, as its benchmark, so it is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No chance-level comparison or model that never saw the knowledge; no direct test of the claim’s specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks. The tested memory and tool conditions are not those attacks.
No fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples as a recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis distinguishing blocked access from deletion.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information recovery test.
No method is tested for resistance to the attacks specified in the claim.

relationships.reason: Utility kept (48.7, 50.4 vs 50.2), but forget F1 barely drops (43.5, 47.9 vs 49.8): forgetting far from complete (L-GD-P-F, L-KL-P-F, L-GD-P-R, L-KL-P-R).
relationships.display_finding: GD and KL retained utility at 48.7 and 50.4 versus 50.2, but forget F1 only fell from 49.8 to 43.5 and 47.9.

relation.reason: Reports forget-set and retain-set F1 after unlearning, which bears on version A. The memory and tool results are added context and don't cleanly test B-F.

tranche.reason: A new agent setting (TOFU with memory and tools) with forget and retain results that bear on version A. The parametric part uses GD, KL and NPO rather than RMU, so T2 is arguable, but the agent setting is the study's main aim.

source_check.notes: Table 1 is scrambled in the text but places via prose, Table 2 and Table 3. Only token-F1 answer recovery is measured; there is no chance or floor reference and no erasure analysis. The paper contradicts itself on whether Mem0 and tool stores hold forget facts: the Fig. 1 caption says no record, but Sec 5.2 and Fig. 2 show memory restoring forget content. So memory, tool and Final rows stay unlinked and cannot_determine.

statements.correction: Text gives, as token F1 (%) on TOFU forget05/retain95 (Table 1): Llama-3.1-8B NPO forget 49.8 to 27.0, retain 50.2 to 34.4; Qwen3-8B KL forget 43.6 to 16.8, retain 43.4 to 19.1.

Parametric GD, TOFU forget05 token F1: Llama-3.1-8B 49.8 to 43.5 (delta -6.3 [-7.8, -4.7]); Qwen3-8B 43.6 to 20.9 (delta -22.7 [-24.6, -20.8]). Same method, two families. Both are 8B, so size is not varied. Base scores differ (49.8 vs 43.6). No relearning or fine-tuning attack.
statements.problem: The statement cites this study's rows but gives no number or result from it; all four results described come from other studies (RMU, GA, ELM). The study's model-dependence evidence is missing.

statements.correction: Memory raises forget F1 in 5 of 6 checkpoints (Llama KL falls 47.9 to 45.9). Tool lowers F1 on both splits for all six. Qwen3-8B empty outputs: 23.6-58.0% under Tool, up to 30.0% under Final. Llama-3.1-8B empty outputs: 1.0% or less, with no refusals; its lower F1 reflects 'reduced answer quality in non-empty outputs'. Tool call rates: Llama NPO 41.5% (forget); Qwen 60.5-78.0% (forget, Tool).
statements.problem: Memory numbers are right (5 of 6; Qwen KL 16.8 to 30.1; complete agent 36.9). But 'many empty outputs' holds only for Qwen3-8B, and no tool-call failure count is reported. For Llama the authors attribute lower F1 to answer quality.

reader_labels.reason: Memory raises forget-set F1 in five of six checkpoints, with a pronounced increase for Qwen3-8B KL, but the tested condition is retrieved context rather than a listed recovery attack and scores generally remain below the base reference (rows L-GD-M-F, L-KL-M-F, L-NPO-M-F, Q-GD-M-F, Q-KL-M-F, Q-NPO-M-F).
